get.description: Retrieve a list of currencies from the TCURC table. It supports filtering based on currency codes in either ISO format (unit) or SAP internal format (internalUnit). If no filter is applied, the API returns all available currencies.

parameters.description: The $filter parameter allows you to limit the currencies returned by specifying them in either ISO format (unit) or SAP internal format (internalUnit). If no filter is provided, the API returns all available currencies.For example, You can filter by ISO code using $filter=unit IN ('EUR','USD','INR'). Alternatively, you can filter by SAP internal format using $filter=internalUnit IN ('EUR3', 'AUD3'). However, it is important to note that filtering can be applied either by unit (ISO code) or by internalUnit (SAP internal format), but not both in the same request.
parameters.name: $filter

get.description: Retrieves header information of previously created pricing documents. They are sorted by the date of their creation in ascending order.

parameters.description: When true, the response includes an attribute 'count' inline, containing the number of stored pricing documents after applying the filter operation. The default setting is false.
parameters.name: $count

parameters.description:
Reduces the search results by the given filter.
Supported filter attributes Supported operators Supported values
sourceApplicationEQ or eqAny alphanumeric value
sourceTypeEQ or eqquote_item, cart_item, order_item,product, favorite, quote, cart, order
sourceIdEQ or eqAny alphanumeric value
lockedEQ or eqtrue or false


Filters can be combined with the AND operator. Each clause must appear at most once. The combined filter must be enclosed in parentheses. Note that if any one of the source attributes is null, then the other source attributes are implicitly treated null: (sourceType EQ 'cart' AND sourceId EQ null) is not a valid filter.
Here are some examples:
Single filtersourceApplication EQ 'cpq'
Combined filter(sourceApplication EQ 'cpq' AND sourceType EQ 'quote_item' AND sourceId EQ '10' AND locked EQ true)
To retrieve locked pricing documentslocked EQ true
To retrieve stored pricing documents without sourcesourceApplication EQ NULL
To retrieve stored pricing documents that are not locked and do not have source(locked eq false AND sourceApplication eq NULL)
parameters.example: (sourceApplication EQ 'cpq' AND sourceType EQ 'quote_item' AND sourceId EQ '10')
parameters.name: $filter

get.description: Retrieves a pricing document previously created, identified by the given documentId. This returns the document header data only. Request additional data by providing $select parameter.

parameters.description: Identifier of the pricing document, must be a UUID.
parameters.name: documentId

parameters.description:
Determines the required detail level of the request by providing one or more of the following values, separated by a comma:
conditions (price elements at document level), items (the document data and the item structure), items-conditions (price elements at item level), items-conditions-scale (details of available pricing scales), items-conditions-successfulAccess (attributes of the determined condition records) , items-attributes (pricing attributes at item level), items-customerHierarchy (customer hierarchy information as provided at item level), items-variantKeyFactors (includes variant condition keys and factors as provided from the configuration), items-currencyConversions (include details of currency conversion happened across price elements), items-priceAgreements (include price agreements).
'items' is a pre-requisite for further item specific details. $select=items-conditions, items-attributes, items-variantKeyFactors, items-customerHierarchy, items-priceAgreements would not return any specific details if not used in combination with 'items'.
'items-conditions' is a pre-requisite for further items-conditions specific details.
$select=items-conditions-scale would not return scale details if not used in combination with 'items-conditions'.
$select=items-conditions-successfulAccess would not return successful access attributes if not used in combination with 'items-conditions'.
$select=items-currencyConversions would not return required details if not used in combination with 'items' and 'items-conditions'.
If the parameter $select is omitted, the basic data of the document is retrieved.
parameters.example: conditions, items, items-conditions, items-conditions-scale, items-currencyConversions, items-attributes, items-variantKeyFactors, items-customerHierarchy, items-priceAgreements

cnv.CurrencyConversionResponse.description:
Currency conversion response details

How is the toCurrency-value calculated?

If the exchangeRate-value is positive
toCurrency-value = fromCurrency-value * exchangeRate-value * exchangeRate-toFactor / exchangeRate-fromFactor


If the exchangeRate-value is negative
toCurrency-value = fromCurrency-value * exchangeRate-toFactor * (-1) / exchangeRate-value * exchangeRate-fromFactor


The derived toCurrency-value is scaled based on the number of decimals allowed for toCurrency-unit.

For example: Refer to below table.

fromCurrency-value fromCurrency-unit toCurrency-unit exchangeRate-value exchangeRate-fromFactor exchangeRate-toFactor toCurrency-value
10 EUR JPY 120.88500000000 1 1 
 = 120.88500000000 * 10 * 1 / 1 
 = 1208.850000 
 = 1209
(As JPY allows number of decimals = 0)
100 JPY EUR -120.88500000000 1 1 
 = 100 * 1* (-1) / -120.88500000000 * 1 
 = -100/-120.88500000000 
 = 0.82723249369 
 = 0.83
(As EUR allows number of decimals = 2)


If fromCurrency-value is null, the toCurrency-value is also considered as null and omitted in the response.

graduatedScaleFactor.description:
Graduated scale factor is determined when the scale type is configured as 'D' in the condition type settings. If graduated interval scales are defined as shown below:
QuantityAmount
up to 1 PC30 USD
up to 5 PC25 USD
up to 10 PC20 USD
When 10 units are ordered, refer to the table below to understand how the condition value is calculated:

Quantity RangeCalculation FormulaCondition Value
For 1 PC30 * 10 * 0.1 (condition rate * condition base * graduated scale factor)30 USD
For next 4 PC25 * 10 * 0.4 (condition rate * condition base * graduated scale factor)100 USD
For next 5 PC20 * 10 * 0.5 (condition rate * condition base * graduated scale factor)100 USD
The graduated scale factor is calculated based on the total quantity ordered and the specific quantity for which the calculation is being performed. In the given example, for 1 PC, the graduated scale factor is calculated as 1/10. For the next 4 PCs, it is determined as 4/10, and for the subsequent 5 PCs, the factor is computed as 5/10.

If local currency differs from the pricing condition currency, then a triangular currency conversion will take place, i.e. the condition currency will be converted to the local currency first and then converted to document currency.

graduatedScaleFactor.description:
Graduated scale factor is determined when the scale type is configured as 'D' in the condition type settings. If graduated interval scales are defined as shown below:
QuantityAmount
up to 1 PC30 USD
up to 5 PC25 USD
up to 10 PC20 USD
When 10 units are ordered, refer to the table below to understand how the condition value is calculated:

Quantity RangeCalculation FormulaCondition Value
For 1 PC30 * 10 * 0.1 (condition rate * condition base * graduated scale factor)30 USD
For next 4 PC25 * 10 * 0.4 (condition rate * condition base * graduated scale factor)100 USD
For next 5 PC20 * 10 * 0.5 (condition rate * condition base * graduated scale factor)100 USD
The graduated scale factor is calculated based on the total quantity ordered and the specific quantity for which the calculation is being performed. prc.ConditionRate.description:
Unit and value for condition rate. Input for condition rate differs based on calculation type. 

 For example, 

 For calculation type A (Percentage) the value is a valid decimal number and unit is percentage in ISO format (value = 5.00 , unit = "P1")  

 For calculation type B (Fixed Amount) the value is a valid decimal number and unit is a valid currency in ISO format (value = -10.00 , unit = "EUR") 

 For calculation type C (Quantity), M (Quantity-Monthly), N (Quantity-Yearly), O (Quantity-Daily), P (Quantity-Weekly), the value is a valid decimal number and unit is a valid currency in ISO format (value = 5.00 , unit = "EUR") 

 In case the value doesn't match the plus minus flag from the condition customization the value is negated. 

For example: If the plus minus flag is X (Negative) and value is 20.00, the value will be negated and -20.00 will be used. 
In case plus minus flag is A (Positive) and value is -20.00, the value will be negated and 20.00 will be used.

prc.ConditionRateConverted.description:
The field holds the condition rate information converted to the document currency.

 If the condition currency is P1 or if the condition currency and the document currency are the same, the field holds the same value as in 'rate' field.

 For example: If the determined condition record is 30.00 EUR per 2 PCE, and if the document currency is USD,  then this field holds the value in USD per 2 PCE. 

 In case the 'value' of the condition is manually updated, this field will hold the condition rate in the document currency unit or P1 derived from condition value depending upon the calculation type .

 Note: While creating quotation/order in the backend via order API's unit and value belonging to 'rate' field should be mapped. This field should not be used. If any error occurs during currency conversion, this field will be set to null.

value.description: Value (E.g. 3.47). Value must be of type double with up to 5 decimal places and up to 11 digits before the decimal point.

prc.ConditionRateNormalized.description:
This field is intended for the integration of the Pricing service with SAP CPQ and can go through breaking changes based on new CPQ requirements without further notice. Do not use this field in other integrations!

The purpose of the field "rateConverted" is to return the condition rate in the document currency instead of the condition record currency. The field "rateNormalized" shall not only consider the document currency but shall also convert the unit of measure used in the condition record to the itemâ€™s target sales unit of measure. But "rateNormalized" is not just the converted condition rate, it is more:

The condition value is used as the basis for the calculation of the normalized rate because the condition value is returned in document currency and the itemâ€™s unit of measure.

For quantity-based conditions:The "rateNormalized" field holds the condition rate information derived from the condition value and is normalized to a per sales quantity unit.
rate normalized = condition value / item quantity
If it's a variant condition, the variant factor is also factored into the "rateNormalized."
Moreover, if it's a time-dependent quantity-based condition, the duration factor is incorporated, too.

For fixed amount conditions (calculation type - B): The "rateNormalized" field remains consistent with the condition value.
rate normalized = condition value

For percentage conditions (calculation type - A):
rate normalized = condition value * 100 / condition base
For variant conditions, the "rateNormalized" considers the variant factor.

If the value of "base" is zero, then "rateNormalized" will be same as "rate".

In all cases, changes through (custom) pricing routines, that were applied when calculating the condition value, are also considered when deriving the normalized rate from the condition value.

Example: Consider document currency as USD and sales quantity as 2 PCE (pieces). In the material master, the unit conversion is maintained as 1 PK (pack) = 6 PCE. If a determined condition record is 5 EUR per pack, the response would have the following values:
"base":0.3332PCE * (1PK / 6PCE) ) = 1/3PK => 0,333 packs
"rate": {"unit": "EUR", "value":5.00}5EUR per 1 pack
"rateQuantity": {"unit": "PK", "value": 1}5EUR per 1 pack
"value": 1.890,33PK * 5EUR/PK * currency conversion factor = 1,89USD (for the 2 pieces)
"rateNormalized": {"unit": "USD", "value": 0.95}1,89USD / 2 = 0,945 =>0,95 USD per piece
Please note that rounding discrepancies may arise during manual calculations of the condition value using "rateNormalized". For instance, while "rateNormalized" multiplied by 2 should ideally result in 1.9, due to rounding, the calculated condition value may slightly differ, as shown in the example where it's 1.89.

In the example above, if a variant factor with a value of 2 is present, the condition value will be 3.78, and the normalized condition rate will be calculated as 3.78/2 = 1.89. The same logic applies to the duration factor and graduated scale factor as well.

Furthermore, it's essential to acknowledge that the value displayed in the "rateNormalized" field may not always match the value displayed in the 'rate' field in the SAP ERP or SAP S4/HANA system. This disparity arises because the condition rate is not normalized based on document currency and per sales quantity unit in the back-end system. Consequently, discrepancies may occur between these values. We advise keeping this in mind when comparing and interpreting rate-related information between the frontend and back-end systems.

Note: When creating a quotation/order in the back end via order APIs, the unit and the value belonging to 'rate' field shall be mapped. The field "rateNormalized" must not be used in that case. It is intended only for display purposes in SAP CPQ.

If any error occurs during currency conversion, this field will be set to null.

prc.TimePeriod.description: Contract start, end dates, daysPerMonth and daysPerYear can be provided here via optional input fields. They are used to calculate duration factors for time-dependent condition types with calculation types M-Monthly Price, N-Yearly Price, O-Daily Price, and P-Weekly Price. These factors are applied to relevant condition rates to calculate the condition values for the given duration. If no duration input is provided, factors 1 month, 1 year, 1 day, or 1 week are applied depending upon the calculation type. The applied duration factor is returned in the response of the time-dependent condition records.

daysPerMonth.description:
Sets the number of days per month, that will be considered when calculating the monthly duration factor. Each day of a month exceeding this number will not be counted. If not provided, value 0 is taken, which means that exact days for each month will be considered.

 For example: Let's assume contract start date as 2020-01-01 and end date as 2020-02-15.
If daysPerMonth was set to 30, then derived month factor will be 1.5. 
If daysPerMonth is 0, derived month factor will be 1.5172413793103448 (as 2020 is leap year).

Another example: Let's assume contract start date as 2020-04-15 and end date as 2020-04-30.
If daysPerMonth was set to 0 or 30, then derived month factor for the 15 days in April will be 0.5.
If daysPerMonth was set to 20, then derived month factor will be 0.3, because it is assumed that month ends on 2020-04-20 making it 6 days of 20 days per month.
If daysPerMonth was set to 5, then derived month factor will be 0, because it is assumed that month ends on 2020-04-05, which is before the given start date.

This factor is then applied to condition rate when calculating condition value for corresponding time-dependent condition types.

daysPerYear.description:
Sets the number of days per year, that will be considered when calculating the yearly duration factor. Each day of a year exceeding this number will not be counted and year always starts from 1st Jan. If not provided, value 0 is taken, which means that exact days for each year will be considered. 

 For example: Let's assume contract start date as 2020-01-01 and end date as 2020-02-15.
If daysPerYear was set to 360, then derived year factor will be 0.12777777777777777. 
If daysPerYear is 0, derived year factor will be 0.12568306010928962 (as 2020 is leap year).

Another example: Let's assume contract start date as 2020-02-01 and end date as 2020-02-29.
If daysPerYear was set to 0, then derived year factor for the 29 days will be 0.07923497267759565.
If daysPerYear was set to 360, then derived year factor for the 29 days will be 0.08055555555555562.
If daysPerYear was set to 45, then derived year factor will be 0.3111111111111111, because it is assumed that year ends on 2020-02-14 making it 14 days of 45 days per year.
If daysPerYear was set to 30, then derived year factor will be 0, because it is assumed that year ends on 2020-01-30, which is before the given start date.

This factor is then applied to condition rate when calculating condition value for corresponding time-dependent condition types.

conditionRateNormalized.description:
This field is intended for the integration of the Pricing service with SAP CPQ and can go through breaking changes based on new CPQ requirements without further notice. Do not use this field in other integrations!

The purpose of the field "conditionRateConverted" is to return the condition rate in the document currency instead of the condition record currency. The field "conditionconditionRateNormalized" shall not only consider the document currency but shall also convert the unit of measure used in the condition record to the itemâ€™s target sales unit of measure. But "conditionRateNormalized" is not just the converted condition rate, it is more:

The condition value is used as the basis for the calculation of the normalized rate because the condition value is returned in document currency and the itemâ€™s unit of measure.

For quantity-based conditions:The "conditionRateNormalized" field holds the condition rate information derived from the condition value and is normalized to a per sales quantity unit.
rate normalized = condition value / item quantity
If it's a variant condition, the variant factor is also factored into the "conditionRateNormalized."
Moreover, if it's a time-dependent quantity-based condition, the duration factor is incorporated, too.

For fixed amount conditions (calculation type - B): The "conditionRateNormalized" field remains consistent with the condition value.
rate normalized = condition value

For percentage conditions (calculation type - A):
rate normalized = condition value * 100 / condition base
For variant conditions, the "conditionRateNormalized" considers the variant factor.

If the value of "conditionBase" is zero, then "conditionRateNormalized" will be same as "conditionRate".

In all cases, changes through (custom) pricing routines, that were applied when calculating the condition value, are also considered when deriving the normalized rate from the condition value.

Example: Consider document currency as USD and sales quantity as 2 PCE (pieces). In the material master, the unit conversion is maintained as 1 PK (pack) = 6 PCE. If a determined condition record is 5 EUR per pack, the response would have the following values:
"conditionBase":0.3332PCE * (1PK / 6PCE) ) = 1/3PK => 0,333 packs
"conditionRate":55
"conditionCurrency":"EUR"EUR
"conditionUnitValue":1per 1
"conditionUnit":"PK"pack
"conditionValue": 1.890,33PK * 5EUR/PK * currency conversion factor = 1,89USD (for the 2 pieces)
"conditionRateNormalized":0.951,89USD / 2 = 0,945 =>0,95 USD per piece
Please note that rounding discrepancies may arise during manual calculations of the condition value using "conditionRateNormalized". For instance, while "conditionRateNormalized" multiplied by 2 should ideally result in 1.9, due to rounding, the calculated condition value may slightly differ, as shown in the example where it's 1.89.

In the example above, if a variant factor with a value of 2 is present, the condition value will be 3.78, and the normalized condition rate will be calculated as 3.78/2 = 1.89. The same logic applies to the duration factor and graduated scale factor as well.

Furthermore, it's essential to acknowledge that the value displayed in the "conditionRateNormalized" field may not always match the value displayed in the 'rate' field in the SAP ERP or SAP S4/HANA system. This disparity arises because the condition rate is not normalized based on document currency and per sales quantity unit in the back-end system. Consequently, discrepancies may occur between these values. We advise keeping this in mind when comparing and interpreting rate-related information between the frontend and back-end systems.

Note: When creating a quotation/order in the back end via order APIs, the unit and the value belonging to 'rate' field shall be mapped. The field "conditionRateNormalized" must not be used in that case. It is intended only for display purposes in SAP CPQ.

If any error occurs during currency conversion, this field will be set to null.

durationFactor.description: Duration factor corresponds to the condition's calculation type: M-months, N-years, O-days, P-weeks. Duration factor is applied to the product of condition rate and quantity to calculate the condition value for the given contract duration.

graduatedScaleFactor.description:
Graduated scale factor is determined when the scale type is configured as 'D' in the condition type settings. If graduated interval scales are defined as shown below:
QuantityAmount
up to 1 PC30 USD
up to 5 PC25 USD
up to 10 PC20 USD
When 10 units are ordered, refer to the table below to understand how the condition value is calculated:

Quantity RangeCalculation FormulaCondition Value
For 1 PC30 * 10 * 0.1 (condition rate * condition base * graduated scale factor)30 USD
For next 4 PC25 * 10 * 0.4 (condition rate * condition base * graduated scale factor)100 USD
For next 5 PC20 * 10 * 0.5 (condition rate * condition base * graduated scale factor)100 USD
The graduated scale factor is calculated based on the total quantity ordered and the specific quantity for which the calculation is being performed. In the given example, for 1 PC, the graduated scale factor is calculated as 1/10. For the next 4 PCs, it is determined as 4/10, and for the subsequent 5 PCs, the factor is computed as 5/10.

If local currency differs from pricing condition currency, then triangular currency conversion will take place. First condition currency will be converted to local currency and then to document currency

Pricing procedure is defined in the standard SAP back end. It contains conditions most commonly used for example material prices, discounts, and surcharges, such as freight and tax

externalConditions.description: The external condition allows adding pricing conditions of a different data source other than the condition technique.

quantity.description: Quantity of the line item being processed.

statistical.description: If an item is marked statistical, its values will be calculated but it won't be included in the accumulated values at document level.

subItems.description: List of sub-items of the main item, the structure of subItems is same as the ItemInput.

taxValue.description: The total sales taxes, expressed in the document currency.
